settings.headline: A different application. Three strengths.
settings.subhead: UK-formulated topical preparation gel, made for aesthetic appointments where the gel format suits the procedure better than a cream. Clinical, Advanced, and Professional.
settings.image_alt: Editorial still life of all three Senseless gel tubes on a warm off-white background

settings.headline: Gel suits some procedures better than cream.
settings.body: Gel sits differently on the skin. Some practitioners prefer it for treated areas that need to stay exposed, or for procedures where cream isn't practical. Some clients prefer the texture. Same three Senseless strengths, different application. Choose by procedure, by practitioner preference, or by what feels right at the chair.
settings.image_alt: Editorial close-up of Senseless gel texture in soft warm light

settings.question: Cream or gel — which should I choose?
settings.answer: Strength is the bigger decision. Format is the next one. Cream suits most appointments. Gel suits procedures where the cream format isn't practical, or where your practitioner prefers it. See the format guide.

settings.question: Is gel stronger than cream?
settings.answer: No. The three Senseless strengths (Clinical, Advanced, Professional) carry across both formats. A Clinical Strength gel is the same concentration as a Clinical Strength cream. Choose by format preference, not by an assumed strength difference.

settings.question: When do I apply gel?
settings.answer: Ahead of your appointment. Your practitioner is the best guide for the procedure you've booked.

settings.question: Can I use gel for tattoos?
settings.answer: Senseless is formulated for aesthetic procedures. For body art see our topical numbing for body art guide.

settings.question: Is this a medicine?
settings.answer: No. Senseless is a UK cosmetic product. Not a medicine. Not a pharmacy product.
